#TanlaIntegratedReportFY264About Our 
Integrated 
ReportTanla Platforms Limited (referred to as ‘Tanla’, ‘We’, ‘Us’, ‘The Company’ 
or ‘Our’) is dedicated to championing the digital citizen through trusted 
communications powered by Artificial Intelligence (AI). We view AI as 
more than a technological capability; it is a profound responsibility 
to protect individual privacy, uphold data integrity, and foster secure, 
scalable, and sustainable digital experiences. Driven by a clear sense 
of purpose, we leverage AI to ensure its benefits flow meaningfully to 
customers and consumers alike, safeguarding trust at every touchpoint. 
Our commitment to ethical innovation is deeply embedded across our 
platforms, products, solutions, and operations, ensuring that as we create 
long-term value for all stakeholders, we are consistently protecting the 
people who power the digital world.
This report reflects who we this report reflects who we are and the 
principles that guide every action we take. Governance has always been 
a foundational pillar of how we operate, and our performance speaks 
to that conviction. In FY26, we received recognition from the Indian 
Chamber of Commerce for Corporate Governance, an acknowledgment 
of the culture of accountability we have built over the years. Our S&P 
Global ESG score of 80 in the Governance dimension, against an industry 
mean of just 37, further underscores the distance between our practice 
and the prevailing standard. 
This Integrated Report is a natural extension of that commitment and 
a purposeful act of transparency towards the investors, employees, 
customers, partners, regulators, and communities we serve. Governance at 
Our Core

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26This report covers Tanla’s financial performance across global operations for 
the period from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026 (#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26). It 
includes Statutory Reports and Audited Financial Statements, with economic 
performance data aligned with our financial reports and compliant with 
Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS). The report covers operations across our 
Innovation and Experience Center in Hyderabad, as well as key offices located 
in Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Mumbai, and elsewhere in India.
We evaluate our value creation through the lens of six interconnected 
capitals: Financial Capital, which represents the pool of funds driving our 
economic foundation and shareholder value; Human Capital, encompassing 
the collective skills and commitment of our people; Intellectual Capital, 
consisting of our proprietary AI-native platforms and technological expertise; 
Manufactured Capital, comprising the physical infrastructure that supports our 
operations; Natural Capital, reflecting our dedication to resource efficiency 
and a reduced ecological footprint; and Social Capital, which embodies the 
trust, relationships, and collaborative partnerships we nurture within our global 
ecosystem.
The Tanla Integrated Report FY26 has been prepared in accordance with the 
following frameworks: 
• IIRC’s <IR> Framework 
• Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards 2021 
• United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs) 
• Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR), in compliance with 
SEBI report 
Our alignment with the International Integrated Reporting Council’s (IIRC) <IR> 
Framework covers six capitals, Financial, Human, Intellectual, Manufactured, 
Natural, and Social & Relationship, demonstrating how we generate value in 
the short, medium, and long term. 
This report is designed to communicate our strategy, purpose, and performance 
to all key stakeholders. We highlight our economic, environmental, and social 
performance, and showcase the significant programs and initiatives that 
drive sustainable value across our global community. Our goal is to act as a 
catalyst for positive change by dedicating our leadership and the responsible 
application of AI to empower the digital citizen. We are committed to fostering 
growth that is inherently ethical, building enduring stakeholder trust, and 
driving technology-led innovation that scales in service of a safer, more 
connected, and purpose-driven world for consumers and businesses alike. 
Forward-Looking Statement: This report may contain forward-looking 
statements. Any statements other than those of historical fact are considered 
forward-looking and are inherently subject to risks and uncertainties, some 
of which cannot be predicted or quantified. By receiving this report, you 
acknowledge that you will be solely responsible for your own assessment of the 
market and our market position and for forming your own view of the potential 
future performance of our business. 
We are fully committed to maintaining regular updates of our performance in 
subsequent years. We will continue to expand the scope of our disclosures in 
alignment with evolving global standards around transparency, governance 
and sustainable impact.
We value and welcome stakeholder feedback on the information presented 
in this report. Your insights help us improve and refine our approach year after 
year. Please write to us at ir@tanla.com.What this

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26
Theme of 
the Year
Protecting the 
digital citizenDigital connectivity was heralded as a paradigm of inclusion and 
opportunity, yet it has devolved into a volatile theatre of systemic 
fraud, impersonation, and pervasive digital exploitation. As synthetic 
threats, ranging from deceptive financial alerts and intercept traps to 
sophisticated identity theft, have surged, digital trust has transitioned 
into the most critical frontier of the modern economy 
We recognized this shift early and acted before it became a mainstream 
concern. In 2023, we built and patented a solution designed specifically 
to address spam and scam at the root. We moved beyond detection to 
prevention and beyond isolated filters to system-level protection. When 
digital scams threatened hundreds of millions of users, Tanla engineered 
the solution and executed the regulatory sandbox, securing results 
that garnered significant attention from the telcos of the nation. It was 
a foundational step in demonstrating that large-scale, compliant, and 
real-time protection was achievable as required. 
Broad-based adoption at the ecosystem scale has been slower than 
the pace of the threat itself. While fragmentation and legacy systems 
pose challenges to universal implementation, we have remained focused 
on our mission, ensuring that these systemic hurdles do not impede our 
innovation or our drive to secure the ecosystem. 
We continued to refine, strengthen, and adapt the solution to enhance 
accuracy, scalability, and resilience against newer forms of fraud. 
This persistence enabled us to successfully deploy Wisely.ai in a new 
geography. There, it delivered a tangible, measurable impact by shielding 
hundreds of millions of users from malicious actors and restoring their 
confidence in digital communications. 
We remain anchored in this objective. Our commitment is to pre-empt 
emerging risks by designing high-impact, real-world solutions that deploy 
protection where it matters most. Thus, protecting the digital citizen is 
not a finite intervention. It is a continuous responsibility that demands 
constant innovation, deep collaboration, and execution at scale.

We see that digital connectivity is an essential part of daily life for 
Indonesians. As digital communications continue to grow, ensuring 
a trusted and secure digital experience is a core responsibility for us. 
Through collaboration with technology partners like Tanla, we are 
delivering more proactive and adaptive protection. AI technology in 
our network helps filter threats before they can impact our customers.
One of the things I like about Tanla is the ability to deliver solutions. The 
anti-phishing tool has some very interesting capabilities. It operates 
on the DLT platform and scans SMS messages to identify where they 
originate from. It also verifies links by collecting data to determine 
whether they are genuine or fake. Using AI and keyword analysis, it 
helps detect fraudulent messages and prevents them from being sent 
to potential customers, protecting them from being defrauded. 1
Vikram Sinha
President Director and CEO, 
Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2622Moments That 
Marked FY26 
In February 2026, Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison hosted an Impact Celebration 
in Indonesia, bringing together Komdigi (Ministry of Communication and 
Digital Affairs), Indosat, and Tanla to mark a milestone in the fight against 
spam and scam. In six months, Wisely.ai analysed 11 billion communications 
across 100 Mn users, identified 2 billion threats. The event, titled ‘Solving 
Real Problems. Delivering Real Impact.’, carried national significance. Dr. 
RS Sharma, Lead Independent Director, Tanla, delivered a special address, 
observing that as the Global South moves online, trust becomes the new 
digital infrastructure.
Pak. Nezar Patria, Vice Minister of Communication and Digital Affairs, 
Indonesia, affirmed that initiatives like Indosat’s demonstrate how 
technology can protect society in concrete ways, and called for every telco 
in Indonesia to build a similar protection layer, affirming that what Tanla 
and Indosat had delivered together was a national standard in the making. 
Tanla hosted ‘Beyond the Hype’, a flagship session at India’s first AI Impact 
Summit, held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi in February 2026. The session 
featured a fireside chat between Vikram Sinha, President Director and CEO 
of Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, and Sanjay Kapoor, Board Member, Tanla, 
followed by a panel discussion with Bipin Preet Singh, Founder and CEO 
of Mobikwik, Ratan Kumar Keshu, Executive Director and COO of Bandhan 
Bank, and Neha Gupta Mahatme, Director of Amazon Pay India which was 
moderated by Anshuman Kar, the Chief Customer Success Officer, Tanla. 
The session brought together leaders from telecom, banking, and fintech 
to examine how AI is delivering measurable outcomes, with Wisely.ai and 
Wisely ATP at the centre of that conversation. Wisely.ai: Solving Real 
Problems. Delivering 
Real Impact.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26LBS Case Study Launch 
London Business School published two case studies on the 
Tanla–Indosat partnership in FY26. Case Study A, titled From a 
$5B National Threat to an AI-Enabled Telco Solution: Wisely.ai, 
examines how Tanla and Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison addressed 
Indonesia’s USD 5 billion annual scam crisis through Wisely.ai, 
covering the platform architecture, the B2B2C commercial model, 
regulatory engagement, and the early deployment results. Case 
Study B, titled Tanla’s Wisely.ai: Leveraging the AI-Powered Anti-
Scam Telecom Shield, explores the platform’s commercial and 
societal impact by February 2026, including 2 billion threats 
blocked, 15% ARPU growth, and government endorsement. 
Global Fintech Fest 2025  
Karix, a Tanla company participated in the Global Fintech 
Fest (GFF) 2025 in Mumbai, India’s largest annual gathering of 
financial services leaders, fintechs, regulators, and technology 
companies from over 100 countries. The team demonstrated how 
AI-driven customer engagement, fraud-proof communication, 
and omnichannel orchestration are reshaping digital 
interactions for India’s leading banks, insurers, and fintechs. 
GFF provided a platform to deepen relationships with existing 
partners and engage prospective customers at the intersection 
of financial services and enterprise communications, a space 
where Karix’s capabilities are increasingly relevant. India Mobile Congress 2025 
Tanla participated in India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2025 in New Delhi, Asia’s 
largest telecom, media, and technology forum. Sunil Bajpai, Chief Trust Officer, 
represented Tanla on the panel ‘Building Trustworthy AI in Telecom’, addressing 
how AI-native platforms can deliver user protection at scale while enabling 
innovation, covering AI-driven automation, the zero-click paradigm, and the 
design of responsible guardrails in enterprise communications. Wisely.ai was 
recognised with the Best Made-in-India Telecom Innovation award at the 
event, affirming its position as a platform protecting over 100 Mn users from 
spam and scam, built on NVIDIA GPU architecture, designed and built in India. 
Conversations That Move Business Forward  
ValueFirst’s Conversations series brought enterprise decision-makers, 
technology partners, and channel leaders together across Gurugram, 
Mumbai, and Bangalore to explore the future of business messaging. 
The RCS Business Messaging edition of Conversations, held at Google 
offices, accelerated enterprise awareness and adoption of Rich 
Communication Services, with participants engaging real-world 
deployment case studies and exploring the expanding RCS ecosystem 
alongside Google and ValueFirst representatives. 
The WhatsApp edition of Conversations, held jointly in association 
with Meta, convened enterprise leaders to explore WhatsApp Business 
Messaging as a channel for large-scale customer communication, 
featuring live success stories, emerging trends in conversational commerce, 
and discussions on maximising business impact. Launch of TNeGA on WhatsApp  
Tanla, through Karix, powered the launch of Namma Arasu, the Tamil Nadu 
e-Governance Agency’s (TNeGA) flagship WhatsApp governance initiative, 
unveiled at UmagineTN 2026 in January 2026. The platform integrates 51 citizen 
services across 16 government departments into a single conversational 
interface in Tamil and English, covering payments, certificate downloads, 
welfare schemes, grievance filing, and property services, deployed in under 
90 days. With 200 additional services planned for phased rollout, Namma 
Arasu represents a significant step toward digital-first, citizen-centric 
governance at scale, and a demonstration of how Karix’s enterprise-grade 
platform is being applied to public service delivery in India.

By adopting RCS Business Messaging as both 
a service and information channel, Apollo 24|7 
fundamentally changed how customers interact 
with complex insurance products. The health 
insurance RCS chatbot eliminated the information 
asymmetry that previously caused drop-offs - 
customers could now self-serve policy premium 
estimates, download PDFs, and book expert 
consultations, all without calling a contact centre. 
The result was a 29% uplift in conversions and a 
70.56% improvement in click-through rates. 
The 15.69% improvement in call-centre 
connectivity with qualified leads is particularly 
impactful — it means agents spend less time on 
unqualified enquiries and more time converting 
customers who are genuinely ready to purchase. The RCS chatbot effectively pre-qualifies 
customers and moves them down the funnel 
before any human interaction, improving both 
efficiency and conversion quality. 
The Sum Assured Calculator for life insurance 
addressed a uniquely challenging conversion 
moment: the moment when a potential customer 
needs to understand the financial value of a policy 
before committing. By making this calculation 
instant, personalised and available within the 
RCS chat, Apollo 24|7 removed the biggest friction 
point in the life insurance sales journey — driving 
a 30% engagement rate and 4.8% lead-to-
conversion rate in a traditionally low-conversion 
category.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26Conclusion 
Apollo 24|7’s RCS journey with Karix demonstrates how the right messaging channel can transform 
the economics of insurance sales. By replacing static SMS with interactive, verified RCS experiences,

=== page 49 ===
#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2648About 
Tanla
Every enduring enterprise is shaped by the markets it serves and the 
convictions that precede these markets. Tanla Platforms Limited was 
founded on precisely such a conviction: that mobile communications would 
emerge as the primary conduit of commerce and human connection, long 
before that premise was self-evident to the world at large. In pursuing that 
vision with singular focus and sustaining it through successive cycles of 
technological disruption, Tanla has evolved into a global CPaaS leader 
and an AI-native platform company. 
What has remained inviolable across this journey is Tanla’s institutional
disposition towards greenfield opportunity. The Company has consistently
elected to act on conviction over consensus, to invest in capability over 
category maturity, and to regard every discontinuity in the technology 
landscape as an arena in which advantage can be constructed. That 
disposition is as defining today, in the age of AI-native platforms, as it 
was at inception.
Tanla was established in 1999 by Uday Kumar Reddy in Hyderabad, at 
a moment when India’s telecommunications landscape was on the 
threshold of a structural transformation. Recognising that the SMS would 
evolve into far more than a personal communication tool, that it would 
become the nervous system of enterprise-to-consumer engagement, 
the Company made a decisive early investment in Application-to-Person 
(A2P) messaging infrastructure. Tanla developed and deployed India’s 
first SMSC (Short Message Service Centre), establishing itself as the 
foundational organization for what would, over the following decade, 
become one of the world’s largest messaging ecosystems. Inception 
=== page 50 ===
49
#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26
The conviction was architectural. Rather than positioning itself as a commodity infrastructure vendor, Tanla from its 
earliest years invested in proprietary technology and talent, building capabilities designed for long-term differentiation. 
This investment culture, in people, platforms, and intellectual property, has been a persistent hallmark of the Company’s 
character across every phase of its evolution. 
Today, Tanla is India’s leading AI-native communications platform provider, with a growing presence across Southeast 
Asia, the Middle East, and global enterprise markets. The company supports more than 2,500 enterprises and maintains 
deep, strategic partnerships with global technology leaders, including Google, Meta, and Truecaller, as well as India’s 
principal telecom operators and a growing roster of international telco partners.
The company’s platforms process over 850 billion digital interactions annually, spanning SMS, RCS, WhatsApp, Voice, 
Email, and emerging AI-driven channels, making Tanla an indispensable part of the digital lives of hundreds of millions 
of end consumers. Its business operates across two interlocking verticals: a Telco business, in which it deploys platforms 
to provide telecom operators with infrastructure, intelligence, and trust, and the Enterprise business, in which it enables 
customers to communicate efficiently and with complete regulatory compliance. 
Across both verticals, our operating philosophy reflects a dual accountability. We design every platform and solution 
with simultaneous regard for two distinct stakeholders: the enterprise and telecom operator we deploy our platforms for, 
and the end consumer that those clients ultimately serve. This commitment to supporting businesses while protecting 
and empowering the individuals they communicate with is an architectural principle embedded in our product strategy,

Tanla’s AI Journey: 
From Intelligence 
to Autonomy 
With artificial intelligence began as a considered 
extension of the company’s foundational belief: 
that the most consequential advantage in 
communications technology would accrue to those 
who could render their platforms not merely faster or 
more scalable, but genuinely intelligent. That belief 
has shaped Tanla’s AI journey across three distinct 
and progressively ambitious stages, each building 
upon the last, representing a more fundamental 
integration of AI into the Company’s product and 
solution architecture. 
Tanla’s first systematic investment in AI was oriented towards augmenting 
its existing platforms with machine learning-driven intelligence. The 
Wisely platform, launched in 2021 in partnership with Microsoft and built 
on Azure’s cloud-native infrastructure, was among the earliest CPaaS 
offerings globally to embed AI and machine learning as core capabilities 
rather than supplementary features. Wise Albert, Tanla’s AI engine within 
the Wisely ecosystem, was designed from the outset to process large 
volumes of communication data, apply Natural Language Processing (NLP) 
to derive intent and context, and deliver actionable insights to enterprise 
clients in real time. 
This phase also saw the Company launch Wisely ATP (Anti-Phishing 
Technology Platform), an AI/ML-based scam prevention solution that 
would, over the subsequent years, earn global recognition for its efficacy. 
Wisely ATP drew upon four distinct AI engines, including Convolutional 
Neural Networks (CNNs), Large Language Models (LLMs), and classical ML 
classifiers, to identify phishing threats across the SMS traffic stack in real 
time. Launched at Mobile World Congress 2023 by the former Chairman 
of TRAI, it quickly established itself as the world’s first end-to-end AI/
ML-based anti-SMS-phishing platform. 
As its AI capabilities mature, Tanla moved to embed intelligence 
pervasively across its product portfolio as a unifying intelligence layer. 
The Intelligence.ai domain emerged as the articulation of this philosophy: 
a suite of AI-driven capabilities encompassing predictive analytics, 
real-time intent detection, campaign optimisation, and omnichannel 
performance intelligence. Every significant product decision in this phase 
was calibrated against a single question: does this investment make the 
platform more capable of learning, adapting, and acting on behalf of its 
users without manual intervention? 
During this period, Tanla also deepened its AI-driven trust infrastructure. 
The Company’s Trubloq platform already the mandated DLT (Distributed 
Ledger Technology) backbone for TRAI’s commercial messaging 
regulations in India was progressively enhanced with AI-powered anomaly 
detection, consent verification intelligence, and real-time traffic pattern 
analysis. The outcome was a platform that not only enforced regulatory 
compliance mechanically, but actively learned to identify emerging 
patterns of abuse and adapt its detection models accordingly.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26FY26 marks Tanla’s transition into its most consequential phase of AI 
evolution: the construction of AI-native platforms, built from first principles 
rather than adapted from legacy architectures. This is the defining strategic 
shift and the one that most sharply distinguishes Tanla’s approach from 
the prevailing industry pattern, in which artificial intelligence is retrofitted 
into existing products as a feature layer rather than constituting the 
foundational logic of the platform itself. 
Wisely.ai, Tanla’s flagship AI-native platform, is the most concrete expression of this philosophy. Architecturally, Wisely 
Ai is designed across three integrated layers. The Data, Infrastructure, and Network Layer processes massive volumes 
of real-time traffic data at millisecond latency fully compliant with local data sovereignty and regulatory requirements 
across all geographies of operation. The Core AI Engines Layer deploys both classical Machine Learning and Generative 
AI models, running on the latest NVIDIA GPU infrastructure, and is responsible for the platform’s detection, classification, 
and prediction capabilities. The Applications Layer translates the intelligence of the two underlying layers into a suite 
of purpose-built solutions for mobile users, telcos, and enterprises each designed to operate with minimal human 
intervention. 
The implications of this architecture are material. A self-learning, agentic platform does not require human analysts 
to identify and respond to new threat vectors. It identifies them autonomously, updates its own models, and deploys 
countermeasures in real time. A platform designed as AI-native from inception scales its intelligence in proportion to 
its data exposure growing sharper, more contextually aware, and more commercially valuable with every interaction 
it processes. This is categorically distinct from the experience of deploying AI as an overlay on legacy infrastructure. AI-Native by Design Stage Three:

fragmented global regulatory environment. This deployment reaffirmed

cannot adequately address. Tanla’s AI-native platforms are designed to 
be structurally ahead of this threat curve: learning new attack patterns 
autonomously, adapting detection models in real time, and neutralising 
fraudulent communications before they reach the consumer at a scale 
and with a speed that no human-supervised system can match.

Message from Founder 
Chairman & CEO
Dear Shareholders, 
We do not participate in market sectors. We build the infrastructure required 
to run a modern digital economy requires.
While the rest of the technology industry fights destructive margin wars over 
standard software features, Tanla has spent years engineered a completely 
different reality. We operate as an N of 1 enterprise. We locate the critical 
vulnerabilities that threaten entire digital populations, from country-scale 
communication fraud to catastrophic financial scams, and we deploy the 
underlying architectural solutions that eliminate them.
Our capability to operate at this sovereign scale is not an aspiration; it is an 
established historical fact. Years ago, we engineered Trubloq to run the Indian 
national switch, processing more than 70% of all A2P transactions across the 
country. We do not look back at Trubloq to celebrate the past, but to establish 
our baseline credentials. We are the only enterprise that has proven it can 
design, deploy, and operate the vital infrastructure underlying a nation’s digital 
communication ecosystem.
Monopolizing the Moat: The AI Nerve Center
We do not view AI as an additive feature or a marketing buzzword. AI is 
the foundational nerve center engineered into the core of every single 
platform we build. From the predictive threat intelligence of Wisely ATP 
to the network-level optimization of Wisely.ai and Wisely Communicate, 
our architecture utilizes advanced machine learning models to analyze, 
encrypt, and secure billions of interactions in real-time. This deep AI 
integration is what keeps our platforms entirely peerless, creating an 
insurmountable technological moat that legacy competitors cannot cross.
This first-mover mandate was validated with the inception of Wisely ATP 
(Anti-Scam). When digital scams threatened hundreds of millions of users, 
we engineered the solution. We pioneered and executed the definitive 
regulatory sandbox, stunning regulators with results that captured national 
headlines from the halls of TRAI.
In doing so, we effectively established an entirely new category of digital 
safety. We are proud to see that our vision has set the structural standard 
for the entire telecommunications ecosystem. When the nation’s leading 
telecommunications giants embrace this exact network-level anti-scam 
positioning and deploy it at maximum scale, it serves as the ultimate 
validation of the market category we created, coalescing telecom partners 
and industry giants around the singular, vital mission of protecting hundreds 
of millions of digital citizens. Today, Wisely ATP continues to deliver that same 
uncompromised safety directly to the users of the world’s leading financial 
institutions.
To understand our current scale and future velocity, our shareholders must 
look at the two distinct, world-class engines operating under our roof: the 
Innovation Engine and our Go-To-Market Highway.
The Engine and the Highway: Monetizing Global Scale
Karix and ValueFirst are our go-to-market engines. Karix is among the 
world’s largest enterprise communication platforms, processing over 850+ Bn 
interactions annually. Karix owns deep enterprise relationships, orchestrates 
high-velocity customer onboarding, and dominates commercial market share 
globally.
The true power of our business model lies in how these two forces integrate. 
Karix captures massive global enterprise distribution, but it launches its 
sophisticated solutioning and drives its omni-channel traffic directly on 
top of the deep, high-margin, AI-driven technological core built by Tanla’s 
Innovation Engine.The Architecture of 
Sovereignty and Digital Trust

The Math of Dominance: Non-Linear Returns
Our financial performance over the past fiscal year is 
the direct mathematical validation of this integrated 
architecture. The strength of our revenue trajectory reaching 
INR 4,418 Cr, our net profit of INR 509 Cr, and our robust 
free cash flow generation of INR 477 Cr are the structural 
outcomes of a non-linear business model. This was further 
reflected in a margin expansion of 50 bps this financial year, 
driven primarily by increased adoption of our innovative 
platforms, proof that as platform penetration deepens, 
financial efficiency follows.
Standard businesses scale their operational overhead 
linearly in tandem with their volume. We reject that model. 
Because we own the underlying infrastructure core, once 
a platform is built and deployed, processing billions of 
additional secure transactions incurs near-zero incremental 
operational cost. This architecture delivers an incredibly 
resilient margin profile, with an EBITDA margin of 16.4% this 
past year.
Furthermore, we do not treat our financial success as a 
historical footnote. We treat it as strategic capital. The 
robust free cash flows generated by our business this 
past year have given us the uncompromised balance 
sheet strength to invest intensely back into our own high-
conviction platforms. This exact financial engine is what 
funded our massive, multi-platform international expansion 
this year.
The Blueprint: Exporting Sovereign Platforms 
Internationally
As we look to the horizon, our forward growth narrative is 
ironclad: exponential value creation will be driven by Tanla’s 
proprietary platforms, while Karix serves as our high-velocity 
vehicle for commercial monetization outside India.
We have successfully proven the absolute power of this 
blueprint in Indonesia, deploying two distinct platforms 
under two highly sophisticated monetization models:
• Wisely.ai (Direct SaaS Value):  Indosat is our direct 
enterprise partner. They pay us a direct SaaS stream 
to embed an AI-native nerve center into their network 
infrastructure, actively protecting over 100 million digital 
citizens from billions of malicious scam interactions.
• Wisely Communicate (Ecosystem Network Share):  We 
have partnered with all major telecommunications carriers 
across the nation, securing a structural, multi-carrier 
revenue share on the underlying network traffic. 
With this sovereign infrastructure established across 
Indonesia, Karix enters the market as our commercial 
highway, launching advanced enterprise solutions directly 
on top of Wisely Communicate and capturing high-value 
local margins. This is the definitive operational model of 
our global future: Tanla’s Innovation Engine secures the 
sovereign platform infrastructure, while Karix drives the 
enterprise traffic down the highway.
This execution is anchored by three immutable platform 
doctrines that we deploy across every market we enter:
We Protect:  We eliminate malicious spam and financial 
scams at the network layer, defending hundreds of millions 
of digital citizens from systemic vulnerabilities.
We Enhance Experience:  We utilize deep SDK integration to 
optimize healthy, high-value, and seamless communication 
directly on the user’s handset.
We Build Brand:  We cement the trust, security, and 
reputational equity of enterprises, telcos, and regulators 
simultaneously.The LBS Verdict: Our Architecture Is the Global 
Masterclass
Our ability to engineer these borderless paradigm shifts 
is no longer just a corporate claim, it is a subject of global 
academic study. London Business School (LBS) has published 
a definitive case study analyzing how our deployment of 
Wisely.ai successfully established a national telecom shield 
in Indonesia,  mitigating a multi-billion-dollar financial fraud 
crisis. When the world’s elite business minds are actively 
codifying your operational blueprint as the definitive global 
standard for AI-driven national security, your technological 
dominance is undisputed.
Our Only Metric: We Promise, We Deliver
At Tanla, we are fundamentally obsessed with impact. We do 
not participate in the corporate theater of over-promising 
and under-delivering. Our reputation among enterprises 
and regulators has been forged on a single, binary metric: 
we promise, and we deliver. When we deploy a platform, 
it is engineered to function flawlessly at immense national 
scale from day one, converting complex technology into 
immediate, undeniable financial and operational results 
for our partners.
Institutionalizing Innovation: The Next Frontier of 
Digital Trust
True platform companies do not rest on historical milestones; 
they turn innovation into a predictable, repeatable process. 
We maintain an aggressive, continuous pipeline of platform 
development designed to anticipate the next structural 
shifts in the digital economy.
Currently, our Innovation Engine is finalizing the foundational 
architectures for our next generation of proprietary platforms. 
Chief among these initiatives is a unified compliance and 
privacy framework engineered to secure explicit consumer 
autonomy across all channels of digital interaction. Built to 
serve as the definitive trust layer for a market of over one 
billion digital citizens, this upcoming architecture will act as 
a critical checkpoint deployed across telecommunications 
networks and major enterprises alike, the new digital 
highway for consumer trust. We are not waiting for future 
regulatory and privacy challenges to arrive; we are already 
constructing the concrete infrastructure to manage them.
Talent Density: Zero Tolerance for Mediocrity

=== page 63 ===
#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2662Stakeholder 
Engagement 
Creating value for stakeholders is the central reason for an organisation’s 
existence. At Tanla, our stakeholders are essential partners in our journey 
whether it is customers, employees, investors, or suppliers, their voices 
shape our decisions. Our stakeholder engagement is built on the bedrock 
of trust and transparency, helping us navigate the social, environmental, 
and economic landscape in ways that are mutually fruitful. 
Stakeholders are identified through a structured process that assesses 
their level of influence, expectations, and relevance to our operations, 
based on factors such as impact, legitimacy, urgency, and diversity of 
perspectives. This identification enables us to prioritise material issues 
that are critical to both our stakeholders and our long-term sustainable 
success. 
Engagement with stakeholders is carried out at defined intervals, 
supplemented by continuous interactions , ensuring a responsive 
and inclusive approach. There is a primary internal custodian for each 
stakeholder group who is responsible for structuring feedback loops. 
Periodic Board reviews, held at least once a quarter, incorporate inputs 
from functional heads representing each stakeholder group, ensuring that 
stakeholder insights flow through to the highest level of governance.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2672Revenue grew by 9.7% YoY to INR 4,418 Cr in FY26, driven 
by organic growth in existing customers and net new 
customer additions. Over the past five financial years, it 
recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.4%. Free cash flow generated during FY26 was INR 477 Cr, 
representing 94% of profit after tax. Over the last three years, 
free cash flow conversion has consistently remained above 
75% of profit after tax, reflecting disciplined working capital 
management, efficient capital allocation and the cash-
generative nature of the business.
During the three-year period FY24 to FY26, 45% of free cash 
flow generated was returned to shareholders through a 
combination of dividends and buybacks. In FY26, an interim 
dividend of INR 6 per share and a second interim dividend of 
INR 6 per share were declared, totalling INR 12 per share for the 
year, in line with the 30% dividend payout policy. The fourth 
buyback in five years was completed during the year, with 
2 million shares repurchased at INR 875 per share for a total 
consideration of INR 175 Cr.
Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) stood at 24.2% in FY26. 
We will continue to invest in platform capabilities, AI-led 
solutions and growth initiatives to strengthen trusted digital 
experiences and create long-term value for all stakeholders. Profit after tax grew by 0.4% YoY to INR 509 Cr in FY26, 
with a PAT margin of 11.5%. Over the last five years, profit 
after tax has remained above INR 440 Cr, demonstrating 
its ability to generate consistent earnings across business 
cycles. 
Earnings per share grew by 1.6`% YoY to INR 38.36 in FY26. 
EPS has remained consistent over the last five years, 
demonstrating the disciplined capital allocation and 
ability to generate sustainable returns for shareholdersRevenue Trend (In INR Cr)  Free Cash Flow (In INR Cr)

The organisations that thrive in the digital economy are built on people and 
the capabilities they develop over time. Sustainable growth depends on 
deliberate decisions about who is hired, how they are developed, engaged, 
and retained. At Tanla, that conviction has shaped every ‘people decision’ 
made in the past three years, and in FY26 the conviction has become a 
record that speaks for itself.
In FY24, the 3Cs Framework (Capability, Competency, and Culture) unified 
Tanla, Karix and ValueFirst into a single people architecture, building the 
cultural and operational foundation on which everything since has been 
constructed. In FY25, GROW (Grit, Reimage, Onwards Growth, Win with 
Customer) oriented every ‘people decision’ towards business outcomes, 
giving the organisation a shared language for what performance means 
and reinforcing a culture of ownership, customer-centricity, and continuous 
growth. In FY26, Tanla Foundry introduced five core operating values: 
Innovation, Impact, Excellence, Ownership, and Speed. Each value carries 
a stated principle and an observable behaviour, the standard against which 
every hiring decision, every development investment, and every promotion 
is measured. 
Together, these frameworks represent the evolution of our people 
philosophy. The 3Cs established the foundation for the employee 
life-cycle, GROW established our ways of working, and the Tanla 
Foundry drives innovation with impact across the organization.  
 
At the core of Tanla’s innovation capability is Tanla Foundry, a cross-
functional model that brings together engineers, architects, product 
specialists, and subject matter experts, who are held to a single operating 
standard, platforms that are gigantic in scale, unique in approach, and best-
in-class in quality. The Foundry is the highest expression of Tanla’s innovation 
philosophy. The standard it represents, of relentless technical rigour and 
outcome accountability, is the bar applied across every hiring and capability 
development decision in the organisation.Contribution to UN SDGs High performance is the culture

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2601 | Innovation 
The platforms Tanla builds do not emerge from 
ambition alone. Combating spam at a billion-
message scale, enabling conversational commerce 
across OTT channels, and securing enterprise 
communications through AI-powered verification 
each required something more robust than a 
product vision. They required the right people, built 
to the right depth, working with tools embedded into 
how they operate every day. Innovation at Tanla is 
built through the quality of people, capabilities, and 
systems that support how work gets done.
Innovation starts with Talent: The Architecture of 
Our Innovation Capability
Our core Innovation function, comprising platform 
engineers, AI/ML teams, and technical architects, 
grew to 321 of Tanla’s 1,043 permanent employees, 
representing 30% of employee strength. Every 
addition to this function is evaluated against the 
same technical and cultural bar that governs Tanla 
Foundry membership, because the quality of our 
platforms is closely linked to the quality of talent. 
More broadly, 833 of Tanla’s 1,043 permanent 
employees, 79.9% of the total workforce, sit within 
STEM functions.
Of the 324 permanent employees onboarded across the organisation in FY26, 79% joined STEM functions, a ratio sustained across 
three consecutive years that reflects our architectural commitment to innovation. Every significant hiring decision reinforces the 
technical DNA of the organisation, and the capacity to innovate is built through the sustained, systematic injection of technical 
builders into the organisation’s deepest structures. Our commitment to building a world-class team is clear from the quality of 
people joining us. Out of all our new hires this year, about 12%, or 38 people, came from top-ranked universities. By placing nearly 90% 
(33) of these Tier one hires into technical positions, we are directly investing in the expertise needed to drive our future innovation.  
 
Greenfield Hiring: Building a Team from Zero in Indonesia
In FY26, Tanla deployed its platform in Indonesia, laying the groundwork for the Wisely.ai launch with Indosat. Establishing a local 
presence required building a workforce from the ground up within compressed timelines, leaving little room for a conventional 
hiring funnel. Demonstrating an innovation-first approach, the team deployed an internally developed chatbot that screened 
candidates and routed them through the process faster. Time from sourcing to onboarding dropped significantly leverages its 
own technology capabilities to solve operational challenges and accelerate business expansion.
Building Capability at Scale
Innovation depends on the continuous development of technical capability. During FY26, Tanla invested in targeted programmes 
designed to strengthen engineering depth and operational readiness in critical technology domains. The rigour of Tanla’s 
technical capability investment is measured through outcome validation rather than completion rates. Two named technical 
cohorts anchor this discipline, each measured against the specific gap it was built to close, and their FY26 results set a benchmark.
I have had the privilege of building systems that matter at 
scale, the Anti-Spam Android and iOS Apps are protecting 
millions of customers every day, and that throughput has been 
holding from month one. A first-principles culture made the 
path from discovery to delivery genuinely fast, and the same 
mindset is what allowed us to deliver Wisely Ai in three months 
with a team that was nearly 60% new. Thankful to all senior 
leaders who backed us without flinching, a buddy system 
and induction culture that helped new joiners contribute from 
week one, and the quiet confidence at the Garage that great 
engineering wins, those were the real differentiators that 
moved the mountain for us.Piyush Kaushik
Senior Product Manager
At Tanla, engineers are empowered to move beyond building technology and become 
creators of business impact at scale. From product vision and platform architecture 
to mission-critical production systems, the ownership entrusted to engineering 
teams is extraordinary. In my journey here, I have had the opportunity to lead multiple 
products, build new AI-powered communication platforms, solve complex reliability 
challenges, and mentor high-performing teams, all while delivering solutions that 
power millions of digital interactions. This combination of trust, innovation, and end-
to-end ownership makes Tanla a place where engineers can accelerate their growth, 
expand their leadership, and help define the future of digital communications.Koushik Das

AI-Native Ways of Working
Tanla’s AI strategy is focused on adoption. The objective is to embed AI into daily workflows and enable employees to solve 
problems faster, improve productivity, and accelerate innovation. Access to AI tools is no longer a differentiator. What separates 
organisations now is depth of adoption: whether AI is genuinely embedded in how people think and work, or just another tool 
they open occasionally.
In FY26, Tanla activated 225 professionals across four Cache Refresh, Tanla’s internal learning and knowledge-sharing 
initiative focused on emerging technologies, AI tools, and evolving ways of working. Through expert-led sessions, practical 
demonstrations, and peer learning, the programme helps employees rapidly build new skills, adopt innovative technologies, 
and apply them effectively in their day-to-day work. These sessions aided cohorts who attended training sessions, changed 
their workflows, and use AI to do real work differently.
AI Deployment Cohort
The 90 professionals who built their own AI tools in FY26 represent a structural shift in organisational capability. When people 
move from AI users to AI builders, the productivity ceiling of the organisation changes, the distance between a problem and its 
solution shortens, and the speed at which Tanla can respond to market and customer needs accelerates.

Employee Initiatives: Building the Culture the Values Demand
Values take hold through consistent experience. The people who build boldly are those who feel trusted and connected. We 
advanced a sustained programme of employee-focused initiatives, as detailed below, making its values tangible in everyday 
work and carefully cultivating the engaged culture that drives continuous innovation. 
1. HR Business Partner (HRBP) Connect: Bringing HR Closer to Employees
Tanla strengthened its HR Business Partner (HRBP) model through the addition of 5 HR Business Partners, reinforcing the 
organisation’s commitment to creating a more connected, responsive, and people-centric workplace in FY26. With a ratio 
of approximately 1 HRBP for every 208 employees, the expanded team enabled closer engagement with employees while 
ensuring that people support remained aligned with business priorities.
HRBPs are embedded within business functions and work alongside leaders and employees throughout the employee lifecycle, 
helping translate organisational objectives into individual performance while ensuring employees receive the support needed 
to succeed. Their role extends beyond performance management and goal setting to include career development, employee 
wellbeing, workplace concerns, and employee engagement. By maintaining a close understanding of both business realities 
and employee sentiment, HRBPs serve as a critical bridge between organisational priorities and individual experiences.
To sustain meaningful engagement across a geographically distributed workforce, HRBPs committed to connecting with at 
least 80% of employees within their assigned population every month. These interactions took place through one-on-one 
discussions, team connects, skip-level conversations, and regular visits to offices across locations. The resulting insights 
enabled early identification of concerns, timely interventions, and more informed people decisions, contributing to a workplace 
where employees feel supported, valued, and empowered to perform at their best.
2. Launchpad Programme: Enabling Early Success for New Joiners
The ability to innovate at scale depends on helping new employees become productive quickly and confidently. Every 
employee joining Tanla begins their journey through the Launchpad Programme, a structured onboarding framework designed 
to accelerate integration, capability building, and early contribution.
The programme combines induction, role-specific orientation, buddy support, and a personalised learning path. During their 
first 30 -45 days, employees gain access to curated learning content through Udemy, helping them develop the technical, 
functional, and behavioural capabilities required for success.
Launchpad is designed to help employees understand Tanla’s culture, values, operating principles, and ways of working. 
By creating clarity, building confidence, and fostering early connections across teams, the programme shortens the time 
required for new employees to contribute meaningfully and strengthens the organisation’s ability to scale talent effectively.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26783. Building Connection and Belonging
People build better when they feel connected, supported, and free to speak up. Throughout FY26, Tanla initiated to invest 
in initiatives that strengthened employee engagement, fostered collaboration, and reinforced a sense of belonging across 
teams and locations.
HR Open House continued as a monthly forum, offering employees direct access to the HR team in an open and informal 
setting. Through a 30-minute session held each month, employees can raise questions, seek clarifications, share feedback, 
and discuss workplace concerns without hierarchy or barriers. The programme serves as an important listening mechanism, 
helping the organisation remain responsive to employee needs while promoting transparency around policies, processes, 
and organisational initiatives.
To encourage collaboration beyond formal reporting structures, Tanla continued Brew and Bond, a weekly employee 
engagement initiative that creates opportunities for informal conversations and relationship building across functions. By 
bringing together employees who may not ordinarily interact through their day-to-day responsibilities, the initiative promotes 
knowledge sharing, cross-functional understanding, and stronger interpersonal connections.
Employee wellbeing and team cohesion were further supported through quarterly sports events conducted across office 
locations. Activities including cricket tournaments and table tennis championships encouraged healthy competition, 
teamwork, and participation while creating opportunities for employees to engage with colleagues in a different setting.
The organisation also celebrated major festivals and cultural occasions throughout the year, recognising the diversity of 
backgrounds, traditions, and experiences represented across the workforce. These celebrations provided opportunities for 
employees to share traditions, learn from one another, and strengthen relationships across teams, reinforcing an inclusive 
culture where employees feel respected, valued, and connected to a larger community.
Together, these initiatives contribute to a workplace where employees feel engaged, supported, and connected to both their 
colleagues and the organisation’s purpose. By strengthening trust and collaboration, they create a cultural environment in 
which innovation, performance, and long-term organisational success can flourish.
Innovation at Tanla is the product of isolated breakthroughs it is a system consciously built to produce them. A workforce weighted 
decisively toward STEM and technical builders, capability programmes that consistently exceed their own targets, an AI-native 
culture that turns employees from tool users into tool builders, and engagement initiatives that keep teams trusted, connected, 
and energised all reinforce one another. This is how Tanla sustains its capacity to innovate, by continuously deepening the quality 
of its people, capabilities, and systems. As the organisation scales into new markets and embeds AI ever more deeply into how 
work gets done, this architecture positions Tanla to keep building platforms that matter at scale, year after year.
02 | Impact 
A business is only as resilient as its people, and at Tanla, that resilience ripples far beyond our walls to drive true impact. We 
focus on solving real problems to serve all our stakeholders, including enterprises, users, telcos, and regulators. When the teams 
designing, selling, and supporting our platforms reflect the diverse markets we serve, our decisions sharpen and our solutions 
work for a wider world. This alignment builds deep confidence in our ability to execute at an incredible scale by safeguarding 
data and flawlessly processing over 850+ billion communications annually. Ultimately, our workforce is the engine that transforms 
operational strength into sustainable, real-world impact for everyone who trusts us.
At Tanla, we believe that business success is enabled by engaged and empowered

alignment, enhancing employee accessibility, and fostering a more people-centric 
culture. Through initiatives such as goal cascading, HR Open Houses, and holistic 
wellbeing interventions, we have continued to create an environment where 
employees are empowered to perform at their best, grow meaningfully, and contribute 
to the organisation’s long-term success.Ankita Arora
Manager, Business HR

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26Workforce: The Quality of What We Have Built
Tanla’s total permanent workforce reached 1,043 employees across 7 offices in India and internationally as of 31 March 2026, 
up 5.1% from 992 in FY25, with growth concentrated precisely where the business needed it most. Go To Market (GTM) grew 
17.7%, adding 31 net employees to customer-facing teams that expanded customer acquisition capacity, strengthened market 
execution, and accelerated revenue momentum. Innovation grew 3.5%, adding quality to an already high-density technical 
function where rigour matters more than scale. Customer Success grew 2.2%, deepening the organisation’s ability to translate 
platform capability into measurable enterprise outcomes. This growth was delivered through 324 permanent new hires and 82 
contractual additions, with GTM serving as the primary driver of commercial scale-up, while Innovation and Customer Success 
together accounted for 196 of the 324 permanent hires.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2684Talent Acquisition: Building the Workforce with Intent
In FY26, Tanla onboarded 324 permanent new hires 
with every new joiner moving through a structured 
onboarding process covering global and HR 
induction, buddy assignment, and introduction to 
the Code of Conduct, Human Rights Policy, POSH 
framework, and other corporate policies from day 
one. Women representation in permanent new hires 
reached 29% in FY26 against 23% in FY25, a 26% 
improvement that reflects the compounding effect 
of an inclusive hiring strategy.
Talent acquisition in FY26 was concentrated on 
Innovation and Customer Success (see Table 2.1), 
which together accounted for 196 of the organization’s 
324 new hires. Innovation added 100 employees 
while Customer Success hired 96, reflecting 
continued investment in building new products and 
strengthening customer delivery capability as the 
business scales. GTM recorded the highest proportion 
of women hires among all functions, with women 
accounting for 39.0% of new recruits. Innovation also 
recorded the largest percentage increase in women 
hires, rising by 66.7% in FY26 compared to FY25, 
strengthening diversity within technical and product-
focused roles.
A pivotal advancement in FY26 was the deployment of AI-enabled talent acquisition architecture, designed to elevate recruitment 
precision and institutional consistency. Role parameters, candidate profiles, and interview diagnostics were automatically 
codified into specialized evaluation frameworks. This structured approach enabled hiring managers to calibrate candidates 
against explicit competencies while systematically aligning assessments with preliminary recruitment insights. Furthermore, 
interview dialogues were synthesized using large language models (LLMs) to generate objective, high-fidelity summaries. This 
AI integration significantly enhanced document traceability and evaluation integrity across assessment panels, particularly 
during foundational screening phases.
This AI-supported approach standardised candidate assessment and strengthened decision-making rigor, resulting in a 50% 
improvement in the conversion of qualified candidates. Furthermore, it compressed the end-to-end timeline to an average 
of 38 days from requisition to offer, comfortably outperforming the SHRM global industry benchmark of 42 days for complex 
corporate functions. This structural acceleration of hiring velocity was achieved without compromising quality. By embedding 
intelligence into each stage of the hiring funnel, from screening to interview synthesis, Tanla has fundamentally enhanced both 
the efficiency and precision of its talent acquisition architecture.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26Nearly four out of every five permanent employees hired in FY26 joined STEM functions, continuing a pattern that has remained 
consistent over the past three years. This sustained focus on technical hiring reflects the central role that engineering and 
product development play in the organisation’s success. As more technical talent joins the workforce, Tanla strengthens its 
ability to innovate, scale its platforms, and meet the evolving needs of customers.
Human Capital Return on Investment (HCROI)
HCROI measures the return generated per unit of human capital expenditure, calculated as (Revenue – Operating Expenses – 
Employee Costs) divided by Employee Costs.
In FY25, the organization’s Human Capital Return on Investment (HCROI) stood at 3.74, indicating that every rupee invested in 
employees generated INR 3.74 of adjusted operating value. In FY26, this metric moderated to 3.23, a shift primarily driven by 
targeted structural investments in our talent architecture.
During the fiscal year, heightened market competition for senior technical and commercial talent accelerated mobility across 
industry-critical roles. In response, Tanla proactively reinforced its leadership and capability base through strategic, senior-
level talent acquisition, including key CXO appointments. While onboarding these high-caliber leaders deliberately increased 
employee costs relative to immediate operating value, this conscious investment fundamentally secures long-term institutional 
continuity, strengthens capability resilience, and accelerates execution across our primary strategic growth vectors.
This moderation in HCROI therefore reflects a deliberate trade-off between short-term efficiency and long-term capability 
building, with investments directed toward strengthening leadership depth, platform engineering capability, and customer-
facing functions to support sustained growth.

Employee Wellness
Wellbeing Ecosystem: Designed for the Whole Person
Our wellbeing philosophy is anchored in a simple principle: sustained operational performance is only possible when our people 
are physically healthy, mentally resilient, and financially secure. Wellbeing is therefore treated as enabling infrastructure for 
consistent delivery and service reliability.
This approach harmonises the dimensions of mind, body, and spirit into the everyday employee experience. The goal is relevance 
in daily work life, ensuring that health, mental resilience, and financial peace of mind are experienced as integral to daily 
operations rather than as external interventions.
This holistic approach directly reinforces operational resilience. The structural reliability of our platforms is intrinsically linked 
to the cognitive stability and personal wellbeing of our workforce. By proactively mitigating stressors across these physical, 
psychological, and foundational life dimensions, the organisation protects continuity in execution and systematically reduces 
the disruptions that typically arise from unmanaged personal and professional strain.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2686This is complemented by an in-house Chief Health Officer (CHO) who manages primary and preventive care across the 
organization, having directly consulted 400 employees during FY26 while actively promoting healthy living and balanced 
nutrition among the younger workforce. Beyond providing general medical care, the CHO prioritizes women’s health by offering 
specialized support through every life stage, including PMS, maternity, perimenopause, and menopause.
Separately, the CHO extended medical advisory services to provide commercial-free support to approximately 40 parents and 
relatives. This dedicated framework also proved critical during instances of hospitalization of an employee or their family, with the 
CHO providing hands-on navigation and advisory support for the few admissions recorded by our employees and their families. 
Annual health check-ups further support early detection and proactive health management, enabling potential issues to be 
addressed before they escalate into longer-term constraints.
Together, these medical interventions shift the organization from reactive healthcare support to continuous preventive care, 
reducing health risks and strengthening employee well-being, with all services provided by the Chief Health Officer (CHO) at 
zero cost to employees.
Mental health and psychological safety
Through the Mind Over Matter programme, employees have access to counselling and structured mental health support. In 
FY26, this was strengthened by training people managers, led by certified psychologists, to identify early signs of distress and 
respond appropriately within teams.
This expands mental health ownership beyond individual employees to the managerial layer, embedding psychological 
awareness into day-to-day leadership behaviour and reinforcing a culture where early intervention is normalised.
Safety and security assurance
The Women’s Safety Net provides WhatsApp-based monitoring for women employees working late or travelling, supported by 
escort services between 8 pm and 8 am. The system ensures that late-hour mobility is supported through structured safeguards 
rather than ad hoc responses.
This reflects an approach where safety is designed into operating conditions, particularly for scenarios where work extends 
beyond standard hours.
Nutrition and Daily Wellbeing Habits
Designed in collaboration with our Chief Health Officer and nutrition experts, the “You Are What You Eat”  programme integrates 
precision nutrition directly into our workplace food ecosystem. This ongoing initiative features calibrated 700-calorie “Balanced 
Bowls” for lunch (50% veggies, 25% protein, 25% whole grains) and gut-health-optimized snacks for the evening, complemented 
by complimentary body age assessments to provide employees with clear baseline metabolic insights. Backed by interactive 
medical sessions and a feedback system at the cafeteria exits to track daily meal satisfaction, the programme educates 
our workforce on critical dietary benchmarks, including the requirement of 1 gram of protein per kilogram of body weight and 
optimal daily caloric ranges. By shifting from occasional wellness events to structural changes in daily consumption, the initiative 
normalizes healthier habits that directly support sustained operational energy, cognitive focus, and long-term productivity.
Life-stage and Family Support
Support for employees during key 
life transitions is built into workplace 
design. This year, 23 employees received 
flexible working arrangements during 
their pregnancy, while 40 additional 
employees were supported for personal or 
health-related requirements. Specialized 
maternal infrastructure and phased 
return-to-work options enable smoother 
reintegration after maternity leave, while 
young parents are supported through 
flexible arrangements based on mutual 
agreement.
This approach recognises that 
performance stability is closely linked to life-stage stability. By accommodating transitions rather than treating them as 
interruptions, the organisation preserves continuity in careers and reduces employee turnover during high-impact life phases.
Financial resilience support
Emergency financial assistance is available for medical, personal, and education-related needs, including salary advances 
for eligible employees with sufficient tenure.This creates a buffer against financial shocks that could otherwise translate into 
sustained distraction or stress, reinforcing stability during periods of uncertainty.
The wellbeing framework is designed around small, consistent interventions that reduce friction in daily life. Whether through 
accessible healthcare, safe mobility, or nutrition, the objective is to ensure that employees can focus on meaningful work without 
being constrained by avoidable personal impediments.
Employee Benefits: The Safety Net
The group medical insurance programme extends structured protection beyond employees to their families, covering 1,144 
employees and 4,175 dependents, including spouses, children, parents, and parents-in-law. In FY26, the programme supported 
213 settled claims amounting to INR 2.07 crore.
A defining characteristic of the programme is that more than half of total claim value relates to parents. This reflects a 
deliberate design choice to recognise that employee wellbeing is strongly influenced by family health, particularly parental 
care responsibilities that often represent the most significant source of emotional and logistical concern for employees.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY268803 | Excellence
Excellence, in a technology company, is a discipline of continuous construction. It is a standard that must hold at every layer of 
the organisation, long before a line of code is written and long after a product is deployed. Sustaining that standard requires 
deliberate choices: attracting the right talent, continuously developing their capabilities, creating transparent pathways for 
growth, and building a workforce that reflects the breadth of perspectives required to serve an increasingly diverse, dynamic, 
and demanding global market.
Excellence is an individual attribute that contributes to the organisational capability that is systematically built, reinforced, 
and renewed over time. It is embedded into the systems that shape how people learn, perform, grow, and lead. Learning 
builds capability, performance systems translate capability into contribution, engagement mechanisms provide the feedback 
required for continuous improvement, and recognition reinforces the behaviours that create long-term value. Together, 
these interconnected systems create an environment where people are equipped to anticipate it, adapt to it, and shape 
it, strengthening the organisation’s ability to deliver sustained value in an increasingly complex and fast-evolving business 
environment.
Learning and Development: Building 
Excellence Every Day
Excellence is not inherited. It is engineered, 
programme by programme and cohort by 
cohort, through investments that are precise 
enough to close specific capability gaps and 
outcome-focused to measure what changes 
in how people work. In an industry where 
technology cycles are shortening and customer 
expectations continue to evolve; learning 
can no longer be episodic. It must become a 
continuous capability-building system that 
equips people to adapt at the same pace as 
the business itself.
This year we adapted this shift by 
complementing its digital learning ecosystem 
of online onboarding and self-directed 
development with structured, blended interventions built around capability gaps identified through hiring manager inputs and 
the annual appraisal cycle. The objective was to ensure that every intervention addressed a clearly defined business need and 
deliver positive outcomes.
Training Snapshot
Total training hours increased by 19% over a two-year period, rising from 19,759 hours in FY24 to 23,429 hours in FY26. The initial 
sharp increase in FY25 reflected a phase of accelerated capability building as the organisation invested heavily in scaling 
technical expertise, leadership readiness, and business-critical skills.
In FY26, we made a conscious shift, from learning 
as a scheduled activity to learning as a capability-
building system. We deepened technical expertise 
in high-demand areas like GoLang, MySQL, 
Nagios, and Aerospike, launched RAISE to build 
the leadership muscle our managers needed, and 
began building our customer excellence capability 
in partnership with the Santosh Nair Academy. 
Each of these was designed to close a specific 
gap. What I am proud of is not the hours delivered. 
It is the problems our people solved differently 
because of the training.Uma Singh
Director,

Key Development Programs
While numerous learning initiatives were executed across the organization throughout the year, the following snapshot 
highlights a few high-impact training programs that exemplify Tanla’s shift from volume-led training to high-precision 
interventions designed to close defined capability gaps with measurable business outcomes.
1. GoLang & MySQL Technical Depth Programs: The GoLang and MySQL interventions represent the organization’s 
benchmark for technical capability building. Documented in detail in the Innovation section, these programs delivered 
exceptional results, achieving impact scores exceeding 100% and effectiveness ratings above 4.33/5. These outcomes 
are now being institutionalized as the baseline expectation for all future learning initiatives, successfully shifting the 
organization from activity-based learning to outcome-defined capability building.
2. RAISE Leadership Intervention (Reflect, Align, Inspire, Strengthen, Empower):  Delivered over two phases across three 
months, the RAISE program targeted 19 managers (16 men, 3 women) spanning Technical Account Management, 
Project Management Operations, and Provisioning across managerial to senior leadership grades. Phase 1 recorded an 
effectiveness score of 4.57/5, followed by 4.35/5 in Phase 2. The program drove critical business readiness by ensuring 
participants demonstrated sustained improvement in conflict resolution, end-to-end accountability, decision-making 
under pressure, and proactive problem-solving to match the escalating pace and complexity of our business environment.
3. Responsible AI Programmes: Through our ‘Cache Refresh’ intervention, employees were equipped to integrate AI into 
everyday workflows while ensuring secure and responsible deployment. The initiative covered AI-assisted software 
development, knowledge synthesis, autonomous AI agents, Cut the AI Slop, which focused on individual AI governance 
and responsible AI deployment in a regulated enterprise environment, and AI bot development. Together, these 
interventions enabled employees to move beyond AI usage to practical AI creation. In FY26, 225 employees participated, 
including 90 who built functional AI-powered tools, strengthening organisational productivity, accelerating innovation, 
and embedding responsible AI as a core organisational capability.

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY2694Performance: Translating Capability into Business Outcomes
Learning builds capability, but excellence is determined by how consistently that capability translates into measurable 
business outcomes. Sustaining excellence therefore requires systems that recognise performance, accelerate growth, and 
create clear pathways for future leadership. For excellence to become an organisational attribute rather than an individual 
aspiration, organisations must create systems that reward impact, accelerate growth, and provide clear visibility into future 
potential.
To execute this across our permanent workforce, Tanla utilizes a streamlined 9-Box Grid Model. This talent management 
framework evaluates employees across two independent axes: Performance on the Y-axis (current delivery against objective 
KRA and KPI metrics) and Potential on the X-axis (behavioral skills and future growth readiness). Managers assess performance 
monthly and evaluate potential quarterly, automatically plotting team members into a nine-box matrix that rolls up into 
distinct talent management paths.
Figure 3.2: The 3*3 Matrix of the 9 Box Model
Promotion and Advancement Outcomes
The 9-Box grid serves as our primary framework for aligning talent capability with organizational growth. By mapping 
individual performance against long-term potential, leadership can objectively determine vertical movement, cross-
functional readiness, and targeted compensation paths. Individuals fall into one of three distinct advancement tracks based 
on their matrix placement:

perspectives and aspirations of younger generations highlighted the importance of 
building trust, providing meaningful feedback, and fostering an inclusive culture. As part 
of Tanla’s leadership development journey, these insights will help strengthen connections, 
enhance collaboration, and drive sustained team performance in an increasingly diverse 
workplace. Prudvi Krishna Poranki

#TanlaIntegratedReportFY26• High-Potential / Fast-Track:  Clear candidates for immediate promotion and critical succession roles. They receive top-tier 
development and aggressive equity allocations.
• Steady Core / Lateral Growth: Strong performers tracking well in their current bands. Focus is on depth of expertise,

To eliminate subjectivity and recency bias, managers also utilize Stack Ranking of senior roles. This process requires ranking 
team members relative to one another based on a full year of objective data, ensuring no two individuals share the same spot.
Tanla’s performance management system covers all permanent employees through Self Appraisal (skillset mapping and 
business impact assessment), Manager Appraisal (skills, impact, potential, and overall feedback), and SLT, CXO, and CEO 
review and sign-off. Reviews operate across four complementary mechanisms: Management by Objectives, Multidimensional 
Appraisal including 360-degree feedback, Team-based Appraisal, and Agile Conversations. Quarterly reviews are mandatory 
and the formal appraisal is annual. In FY25, 100 percent of eligible permanent employees participated in the appraisal cycle. 
The following data reflects the most recently completed appraisal cycle (FY25), which is standard practice as the annual cycle 
concludes after the reporting period closes at Tanla.
Promotion Rates by Gender
Data over the reported period demonstrates a notable shift from FY23, where the promotion rate for women stood at 5.1% 
compared to 13.6% for men. In the subsequent periods, women registered a higher proportional rate of promotion relative 
to total gender headcount than men. In FY25, the promotion rate for women stood at 19.4% compared to 15.6% for men, 
maintaining a trend from FY24 where the women promotion rate was 22.9% compared to 18.2% for men. This represents a 
consistent percentage rate differential over the last two reporting cycles (+4.7% in FY24 and +3.8% in FY25), reflecting an 
internal talent pipeline where structured capability development steadily translates into career advancement. Following the 
accelerated advancement peak across both demographics in FY24, the FY25 distribution reflects a stabilized, merit-based 
advancement framework aligned with organizational headcount normalization.

Recognition: Making Excellence Visible
In organizations where innovation compounds over time, recognition is a cultural signal that tells every person in the organization 
what performance looks like and what it earns. In FY26, Tanla conferred 214 rewards and recognition to employees across 
the Tanla Group, recognizing 20.5% of our workforce across seven categories spanning individual performance, managerial 
excellence, team achievement, and on-the-spot contribution, ensuring that every form of value delivered has a corresponding 
and visible expression of appreciation.

diversify how it defines and celebrates success. Alongside this modernization, foundational programs like high-tier individual 
recognition under the Star Performer category grew by 12 percent, moving from 82 to 92 recipients. This transition demonstrates 
a healthy high-performance culture in motion: the structural introduction of new categories allowed for more precise tracking 
of everyday excellence, while the flagship individual benchmark remained stringent as more individuals successfully earned 
the right to clear it.

categories to deliver precise, timely, and personalized recognition at every operational layer.
